source_contract: np.sqrt computes real square root over the non-negative real domain. Under the default error policy (invalid='warn'), negative real inputs emit a RuntimeWarning and produce np.nan (dtype float64), preserving the real dtype. np.emath.sqrt automatically extends real inputs to the complex domain when x < 0, returning 1j (dtype complex128) without warning. Under IEEE 754 and NumPy semantics, NaN is unequal to everything (including itself), so np.nan == 1j evaluates to False.
